sg5_contrastive_seed.title: SG5 contrastive cross-attention seed
sg5_contrastive_seed.what: Tests whether contrasting the class-word cross-attention (CA) probability against other prompt positions closes the coverage gap between the class-word seed (seed recall 0.82) and OVAM's released token (0.93) without losing precision. Only the per-head map entering the frozen CA average changes; every seed is then run through the same five fixed pipelines. Training-free for the W-variants; the token variants use OVAM's released token, frozen.
sg5_contrastive_seed.names: Each name is <seed>/<pipeline>. Seeds: W = class word, p_T (mean softmax probability of the class word pieces over the 77 padded prompt keys; frozen convention); WS = log p_T - log p_SoT (contrast with the start token); WK = p_T/(p_T + p_SoT) (class word in OVAM's two-key form); WN = log p_T - log mean of p over all non-target positions; WE = log p_T - log mean of p over <EoT> and padding positions; WY = mean of p_T over the class word and its fixed synonyms (same template; 8 classes have no synonym, so WY = W for them); TC = OVAM released token with keys [<SoT>, token], p_tok (few-shot reference, T-C); TS = log p_tok - log p_SoT. Pipelines: seed = CA map alone, no propagation; REF = one observation-wise SA pass through module 15, mean_i(A_i c); P1 = two passes, mean_i(A_i^2 c); R2 = REF followed by OVAM's fixed DenseCRF (note: here 'R2' alone means REF+DenseCRF); P1+R2 = two passes + DenseCRF (FTF for W). 8 seeds x 5 pipelines = 40 cells.
sg5_contrastive_seed.reference: Four separate screens: W/REF (seed effect under one pass; candidates WS/WK/WN/WE/WY at REF), W/P1+R2 = FTF (candidates the same five at P1+R2), TC/REF (candidate TS/REF) and TC/R2 = T-C few-shot pipeline (candidate TS/R2). The seed and P1 cells of non-screened pipelines are reported only.
sg5_contrastive_seed.outcome: The reference won 5/5 folds in all four screens and nothing was frozen (OOF W/REF 0.7873, W/P1+R2 0.8134, TC/REF 0.8496, TC/R2 0.8647). The log-ratio seeds raise seed recall to 0.96-0.98 but cut precision to 0.47-0.67 (Section 70).

sg1_sg3_graph_refinement.title: SG1/SG3 anchored graph refinement
sg1_sg3_graph_refinement.what: Asks whether confident foreground/background anchors can keep the object completion of SA propagation while limiting leakage. SG1 solves a foreground-before-background absorbing walk (hitting probability) on the mean SA graph; SG3 is a finite-step confidence-locked baseline. The anchor quantiles, an optional image-border background band and (for SG3) the number of steps are varied, on both the class-word (W) and released-token (T) tracks.
sg1_sg3_graph_refinement.names: <track>/<family>/f<FF>_b<BB>_r<R>[_n<N>]. Track W = class-word CA seed, T = OVAM released token. The graph is the mean row-stochastic SA affinity (all 31 calls x 8 heads of module 15). fFF = foreground anchors are pixels at or above quantile 0.FF of the min-max-normalized 64x64 seed (f80/f90/f95 = top 20/10/5%). bBB = background anchors at or below quantile 0.BB (b05/b10 = bottom 5/10%). rR = border width: r0 none, r1 also adds a one-pixel image border to the background anchors (foreground wins at overlap). SG1 = clamp anchors to 1/0 and iterate the mean graph, re-clamping each step, until max change < 1e-4 or 200 iterations. SG3 = start from the CA seed, apply nN mean-graph steps (n1 or n2), restoring the original CA values at both anchor sets after each step. REF = observation-wise one pass mean_i(A_i c); P1 = observation-wise two passes mean_i(A_i^2 c). 12 SG1 + 24 SG3 + 2 references = 38 cells per track, 76 total.
sg1_sg3_graph_refinement.reference: W/REF for screens W-SG1 and W-SG3, T/REF for T-SG1 and T-SG3 (each family screened independently against its track's one-pass map). P1 is recomputed and reported only.
sg1_sg3_graph_refinement.outcome: No family met the 4/5 rule; W-SG1, W-SG3 and T-SG1 kept REF 5/5 (OOF 0.7873 word, 0.8507 token); T-SG3 kept T/REF with 3/5 votes (candidate chosen in 2 folds, selected-path OOF 0.8507 -> 0.8534, +0.0027). Best token cell T/SG3/f95_b05_r0_n1 led to the locked confirmation (Section 72).

sg8_observation_consensus.title: SG8 observation-consensus propagation
sg8_observation_consensus.what: Asks whether agreement among the 248 individual SA observations (31 denoising calls x 8 heads of module 15) identifies pixels where propagation is reliable. Each z_i = A_i c is computed separately (affinities are never averaged before propagation) and combined by four independent families: robust aggregation, variance-guided retention of the seed, symmetric sign agreement, and expansion-only agreement. Screened separately on the class-word (W) and released-token (T) tracks.
sg8_observation_consensus.names: <track>/<family>/<parameter>; track W = class word, T = OVAM released token. REF = ordinary mean mu = mean_i z_i (one pass). A = per-pixel robust aggregate instead of the mean: trim10 / trim20 = trimmed mean removing floor(0.1*248)=24 / floor(0.2*248)=49 observations from each tail; median = median (mean of the two central values). B/tauXpYY = variance-guided CA retention, u*c + (1-u)*mu with u = sigma/(sigma+tau), sigma = per-pixel population std of the z_i; tau in {0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20} ('p' = decimal point). C/rhoXpYY = symmetric sign agreement: mu where r_up >= rho or r_down >= rho, else keep the seed c, where r_up / r_down = fraction of observations with z_i > c / z_i < c; rho in {0.60, 0.70, 0.80, 0.90}. D/rhoXpYY = expansion-only agreement: max(c, mu) where r_up >= rho, else c; same rho values. 16 cells per track, 32 total.
sg8_observation_consensus.reference: W/REF and T/REF (the ordinary observation-wise one-pass mean); each family A-D is its own screen against its track's REF.
sg8_observation_consensus.outcome: Two screens froze. W-C froze W/C/rho0p80 (4/5, OOF 0.7875 -> 0.7970, +0.0095; COCO 0.6213 vs 0.6178) and T-A froze T/A/median (4/5, OOF 0.8508 -> 0.8544, +0.0036; COCO 0.6742 vs 0.6683). W-A had a positive path (+0.0067) but only 3/5 votes; B and D lost; T-C kept REF.

sg9_reciprocal_propagation.title: SG9 reciprocal SA propagation
sg9_reciprocal_propagation.what: Tests whether propagation edges supported in both spatial directions are more reliable than asymmetric long-range shortcuts. Each of the 248 per-observation affinities A_i is made reciprocal before a single observation-wise pass; three reciprocity operators are compared with the original A on the class-word and released-token tracks.
sg9_reciprocal_propagation.names: <track>/<operator>; W = class word, T = OVAM released token. REF = original row-stochastic A_i (one pass, mean_i A_i c). R1_geometric = sqrt(A_i * A_i^T) elementwise, then row-normalized. R2_minimum = min(A_i, A_i^T) elementwise, then row-normalized. R3_soft_gate = A_i * sqrt(A_i^T), then row-normalized. Every operator is formed per call/head before propagation; one pass only. 4 cells per track, 8 total.
sg9_reciprocal_propagation.reference: W/REF and T/REF (one track-wise screen each); tie preference R3 > R1 > R2.
sg9_reciprocal_propagation.outcome: REF won 5/5 on both tracks and nothing froze (OOF W 0.7875, T 0.8508). R1/R2 changed full-VOC mIoU only slightly (W 0.7913/0.7904 vs 0.7888) and R3 lowered it (0.7743).

sg10_seed_connected_bottleneck.title: SG10 seed-connected bottleneck propagation
sg10_seed_connected_bottleneck.what: Tests whether pixels that propagation correctly adds are more strongly connected to the confident seed (by the widest-path, max-min bottleneck strength in the mean SA graph) than false-positive leakage. The ordinary one-pass map is kept as evidence and modulated by the rank-normalized bottleneck score; the operator, graph and seed-source quantile are varied on the class-word and released-token tracks.
sg10_seed_connected_bottleneck.names: <track>/<cell>; W = class word, T = OVAM released token. seed = CA map alone; REF = mu = mean_i(A_i c), one observation-wise pass; P1 = two passes (reported only). Candidates <Op>_<G>_q<QQ>: qQQ = seed sources S_F are pixels with c >= the QQth percentile (q90/q95 = top 10/5%), used as sources only, never clamped. G1 = mean affinity A_bar as a directed graph; G2 = sqrt(A_bar * A_bar^T) (symmetric). Bn = exact widest-path strength from S_F on the dense 4096-node graph, converted to percentile rank (frozen from a smoke test before any score). Op: B1 = mu*Bn; B2a25 / B2a50 = mu*(alpha + (1-alpha)*Bn) with alpha 0.25 / 0.50; B3 = c + Bn*(mu - c) where mu > c, else mu (expansion gated by connectivity). L_<Op>_q<QQ> = the same operators on a local graph (G2 weights restricted to 4-neighbour edges); diagnostic only, never selectable. 16 candidates + seed, REF, P1 + 8 L cells = 27 per track, 54 total.
sg10_seed_connected_bottleneck.reference: W/REF for SG10-W and T/REF for SG10-T, over the 16 candidates each (seed, P1 and L_* are reported only).
sg10_seed_connected_bottleneck.outcome: The reference won 5/5 in both screens and nothing froze (OOF W/REF 0.7873, T/REF 0.8496). The best cell, B3, stays below REF (W 0.7824-0.7827 vs 0.7886), and the bottleneck AUC for new TP vs new FP is at or below chance (Section 79).

sg2_consensus_edges.title: SG2 consensus-edge SA graph
sg2_consensus_edges.what: Tests whether reweighting each SA edge by how consistently the 248 observations agree on it reduces leakage while keeping object completion. Edges are reweighted, never pruned, by a reliability score r raised to a power gamma, either in one consensus mean graph or per observation, with one or two propagation passes; run on class-word and released-token tracks (the token track is diagnostic only under Section 82).
sg2_consensus_edges.names: <track>/<form>_<rel>_g<GG>_n<N>; W = class word, T = OVAM released token (diagnostic). rel = per-edge reliability: cv = mean_i A_i / sqrt(mean_i A_i^2) = 1/sqrt(1+CV^2) (1 when all observations agree); occ = (number of observations with A_i(p,q) > 1/4096, plus 0.5) / 249 (share of observations where the edge is above uniform). gGG = exponent gamma: g05 = 0.5, g10 = 1, g20 = 2; weights A * r^gamma. form: G = one consensus graph W = rownorm(A_bar * r^gamma), map W c (n1) or W(W c) (n2); O = per observation A~_i = rownorm(A_i * r^gamma), map mean_i A~_i c (n1) or mean_i A~_i^2 c (n2). nN = passes (1 or 2). Other cells: seed = CA alone; REF = mean_i(A_i c); P1 = mean_i(A_i^2 c); MG2 = A_bar^2 c (mean graph squared; diagnostic). 24 candidates + 4 = 28 per track, 56 total.
sg2_consensus_edges.reference: Four screens: one-pass candidates (n1) against REF and two-pass candidates (n2) against P1, per track. Tie order gamma 0.5 > 1 > 2, then cv > occ, then G > O.
sg2_consensus_edges.outcome: SG2-W-1pass froze W/G_cv_g20_n1 (5/5, OOF 0.7873 -> 0.7984, +0.0111; COCO 0.6234 vs 0.6173, paired +0.0158 [+0.0129, +0.0187]); SG2-W-2pass kept W/P1 (0.7997). The token diagnostic also froze T/G_cv_g20_n1 (0.8496 -> 0.8568); T 2-pass kept T/P1. The frozen one-pass cell matches, but does not beat, P1 (0.8005 full VOC).

sg4_region_labels.title: SG4 SA regions labelled by CA
sg4_region_labels.what: Segments the image into regions using self-attention only (spectral or row clustering of the mean SA graph), then gives each region a single score from cross-attention evidence, producing a piecewise-constant map. Partition type, number of regions K and the region-labelling statistic are varied on class-word and released-token tracks (the token track is diagnostic only). A GT-majority oracle labelling measures how good the partitions themselves are.
sg4_region_labels.names: <track>/<PART><K>_<label>; W = class word, T = OVAM released token (diagnostic). PART: SPEC = k-means on the K leading row-normalized eigenvectors of D^-1/2 S D^-1/2 with S = (A_bar + A_bar^T)/2 (spectral clustering); ROWS = k-means on the L2-normalized rows of A_bar. K in {8, 16, 32} regions (deterministic k-means++, seed 0, 3 restarts, 30 iterations). label: cmean = region mean of the CA seed c; cmed = region median of c; rmean = region mean of the one-pass REF map. seed = CA alone; REF = mean_i(A_i c). 18 candidates + 2 = 20 per track, 40 total.
sg4_region_labels.reference: W/REF and T/REF (one screen per track). Tie order cmean > cmed > rmean, then SPEC > ROWS, then K 8 > 16 > 32.
sg4_region_labels.outcome: REF won 5/5 on both tracks (OOF W 0.7873, T 0.8496); the best W cell SPEC32_rmean reaches 0.7898 vs 0.7886 in-sample. The oracle-labelled partitions reach 0.80-0.88 mean-image IoU on VOC-Sim (SPEC32 0.8761) and 0.61-0.80 on COCO-Cap, so the bottleneck is labelling, not the partition.

training_free_backlog.title: Training-free Track-A backlog (14 families)
training_free_backlog.what: One package that screens the 14 remaining training-free backlog ideas (diffusion kernels, multi-resolution propagation, background suppression, head weighting, DiffSeg-style and query-feature segmentation, SA mean field) against the class-word one-pass reference. Only frozen SD 1.5 class-word CA and module-15 SA (all 31 calls x 8 heads) are used; each family independently selects its parameter and threshold in the five VOC-Sim folds.
training_free_backlog.names: Format <family>/<parameter>; numeric suffixes are the value x 100 as 3 digits (e.g. t050 = 0.5, w1000 = 10). A_bar = mean module-15 SA affinity; c = min-max CA seed. REF/one_pass = mean_i(A_i c). P3/tXXX = heat-kernel diffusion exp(t(A_bar - I)) c truncated at 8 terms (k = 0..8), diffusion time t = 0.5/1/2/4. P5/nK = K = 1..4 applications of the symmetric normalized graph D^-1/2 S D^-1/2, S = (A_bar + A_bar^T)/2. P9/sXXX_bgB = coarse-to-fine propagation through the mean graph of the last SA module at 8 -> 16 -> 32 -> 64 resolution, keeping the confident seed (c >= s, s = 0.5/0.7/0.9) as a floor after each step; bg1 multiplies by 1 - minmax(the same expansion of the start-token (BOS) CA map), bg0 does not. F2/aXXX = REF x (alpha + (1 - alpha) x minmax(column sums of A_bar)), alpha = 0/0.25/0.5/0.75. BG1/gXXX = binary mask REF > gamma x (A_bar applied to the BOS CA map), gamma = 0.5/0.75/1.0/1.25/1.5. W1/TXXX = weighted mean of the 248 observation maps z_i with weights proportional to (1/spatial entropy of z_i)^(1/T), T = 0.5/1/2. W2/kK = average of only the K = 2/4/6 of 8 heads whose call-mean propagated map has the highest Pearson correlation with c. W4/converged = iterate x <- minmax(A_bar x) from c until max change < 1e-4 (max 50 iterations). H1/proportional = one-step propagation of c through the last SA module at each of 8/16/32/64 resolution, averaged with weights proportional to resolution. G1/tauXXX = DiffSeg merging on A_bar (16x16 anchor grid, 3 symmetric-KL merge rounds, KL threshold tau = 0.9/1.1, no k-means refinement); each region scored by its mean REF. G4/sXXX = binary seeded region growing: 4-connected components of neighbouring pixels whose call-mean SA query features have cosine >= s (0.5/0.7/0.9), kept if they contain a CA peak (c >= 0.9). M1/ca_prototype = cosine of each pixel's SA query feature to one CA-weighted mean prototype. M2/kK = k-means (K = 2/3/4, 20 iterations) on query features of the top-20% CA pixels; score = max cosine to the K prototypes. R1/wXXX = 5 mean-field iterations q <- sigmoid(logit(minmax REF) + w A_bar (2q - 1)), pairwise weight w = 1/3/10. BG1 and G4 output binary masks, so the mask threshold does not affect them. 44 cells.
training_free_backlog.reference: REF/one_pass (class-word one SA pass, mean_i(A_i c)), against which each of the 14 families is an independent screen.
training_free_backlog.outcome: REF/one_pass won 5/5 in all 14 screens; nothing promoted (OOF 0.7875, COCO 0.6178). Best full-VOC cells: R1/w100 0.7929 and P5/n2 0.7895 vs REF 0.7888. The label-using diagnostic C1 (per-class thresholds) reaches 0.8348 but is excluded from the label-free pipeline.
training_free_backlog.unsure: The protocol and config say only 'last sorted SA module at each resolution' for the 8/16/32 levels used by P9 and H1; the exact module names were not checked. Operator details (BOS map, 50-iteration cap for W4, CA-peak = min-max c >= 0.9 for G4, top-20% CA quantile for M2) were confirmed in configs/training_free_backlog.json and src/segmentation/training_free_backlog.py, not in the report.

sg11_sg12_observation_reliability.title: SG11 robust consensus and SG12 reliable observations
sg11_sg12_observation_reliability.what: Two class-word-only follow-ups to SG8. SG11 combines SG8's sign-agreement gate with a robust aggregate (median or 20% trimmed mean) in place of the plain mean. SG12 instead keeps only the most mutually consistent SA observations (by mean cosine similarity of their propagated maps to all other observations) and averages those. Each is an independent screen against the one-pass reference, with SG8 cells recomputed as controls.
sg11_sg12_observation_reliability.names: All cells are class-word (W). REF = one pass mean_i(A_i c), no DenseCRF. Controls recomputed from SG8: C/rho0p80 = SG8-C sign consensus at rho 0.80; A/trim20 and A/median = SG8-A robust aggregates. SG11/<agg>/rhoXpYY: per pixel, use the robust aggregate where max(r_up, r_down) >= rho, otherwise keep the seed c; agg = median (mean of the two central values of 248) or trim20 (drop floor(0.2*248) = 49 observations from each tail); r_up / r_down = fraction of observations with z_i > c / z_i < c; rho in {0.70, 0.80, 0.90} ('p' = decimal point). SG12/topNN: rank the 248 observations by mean cosine similarity of their raw propagated vector to all other observations (self excluded) and average the raw vectors of the top NN% (ceil(fraction*248): top50 = 124, top70 = 174, top80 = 199, top90 = 224). 14 cells.
sg11_sg12_observation_reliability.reference: W/REF (one pass without DenseCRF) for both screens; the SG8 controls are reported for context, not as references.
sg11_sg12_observation_reliability.outcome: Recovered after the finalizer audit (Sec. 89), from within-package V100 comparisons: SG11 froze W/SG11/trim20/rho0p80 (5/5, OOF 0.7873 -> 0.7984, +0.0111; COCO 0.6219 vs 0.6172) and SG12 froze W/SG12/top50 (5/5, OOF 0.7873 -> 0.7967, +0.0094; COCO 0.6272).

sg2_densecrf_confirmation.title: Locked SG2 + DenseCRF confirmation
sg2_densecrf_confirmation.what: A locked confirmation (no parameter search) of whether the promoted one-pass SG2 consensus graph, followed by OVAM's fixed DenseCRF, beats the final training-free pipeline FTF (two passes + DenseCRF). Six cells are computed from each single generation.
sg2_densecrf_confirmation.names: All class-word (W). REF = mean_i(A_i c); P1 = mean_i(A_i^2 c); SG2 = the Section 85 winner W/G_cv_g20_n1 exactly: G = rownorm(A_bar * r^2), r = mean_i A_i / sqrt(mean_i A_i^2), map G c. +R2 = followed by OVAM's fixed DenseCRF on the thresholded mask; P1+R2 = FTF.
sg2_densecrf_confirmation.reference: Primary: W/P1+R2 (FTF), candidate W/SG2+R2. Secondary: W/REF+R2, isolating SG2's contribution under identical postprocessing. The no-CRF cells check that SG2 reproduces.
sg2_densecrf_confirmation.outcome: Recovered after the finalizer audit (Sec. 89): primary kept FTF with 0/5 candidate votes; locked SG2+R2 OOF 0.8111 vs FTF 0.8132 (-0.0021); COCO 0.6261 vs 0.6371. Secondary vs REF+R2: +0.0064 OOF (0.8047 -> 0.8111) but only 2/5 votes, so W/REF+R2 stays frozen.

sg13_target_region_inference.title: SG13 target-conditioned region labelling
sg13_target_region_inference.what: Tests whether simple target-conditioned scores can label the fixed SPEC32 SA regions well enough to recover SG4's oracle headroom. Three fixed region-scoring rules (no learned components) threshold raw region scores into hard region masks; class-word only.
sg13_target_region_inference.names: All class-word (W). REF = one pass; P1 = two passes; SG4/SPEC32_rmean = legacy SG4 control (32 spectral regions, region mean of REF, min-max then bilinear, thresholds 0.30-0.70); C/rho0p80 = SG8-C consensus control. SG13/R1-R3 on the same SPEC32 partition, with per-region C = mean c, P = mean of raw one-pass mu, Q = mean of q = max(fraction z_i > c, fraction z_i < c), M = max c: R1 = P; R2 = P*Q; R3 = 0.5*M + 0.5*P*Q. The raw region score is thresholded (grid 0-1 in steps of 0.005), then region labels are nearest-expanded to annotation size. 7 cells.
sg13_target_region_inference.reference: W/REF; R1, R2, R3 screened individually and as a joint family (tie order R1 > R2 > R3).
sg13_target_region_inference.outcome: All four screens (R1, R2, R3, joint) kept W/REF 5/5, OOF 0.7875, gain 0. Full-VOC R1/R2/R3 = 0.7685/0.7537/0.7039 vs REF 0.7888; the same-generation majority oracle is 0.8758 (VOC) and 0.7928 (COCO) mean-image IoU.
sg13_target_region_inference.unsure: The report also lists a 'Historical selected SG2 (Section 85)' row (0.7984/0.6234); it is a copied historical comparator, not a configuration recomputed in this package.

sg12_crf.title: Locked SG12 + DenseCRF confirmation
sg12_crf.what: Locked confirmation of whether the frozen SG12 top-50% observation filter, followed by the fixed OVAM DenseCRF, beats the final training-free pipeline FTF (two passes + DenseCRF). No CRF or SG12 parameter is tuned.
sg12_crf.names: All class-word (W). REF = mean_i(A_i c); P1 = mean_i(A_i^2 c) (observation-wise, not (mean A)^2 c); SG12/top50 = mean of the raw propagated maps of the 124 of 248 observations with the highest leave-one-out mean cosine similarity to the others; +R2 = fixed OVAM DenseCRF (parameters 10, 80, 13, 3, 3, 5) on the thresholded mask. P1+R2 = FTF. 5 cells.
sg12_crf.reference: W/P1+R2 (FTF); candidate W/SG12/top50+R2. Unrefined SG12 is diagnostic.
sg12_crf.outcome: Protocol kept W/P1+R2 5/5; forced candidate OOF 0.811526 vs FTF 0.813209 (-0.0017); full VOC 0.813126 vs 0.813209; COCO 0.631503 vs 0.637141.

sg14.title: SG14 SG11 x SG12 complementarity
sg14.what: Tests whether SG12 (dropping globally unreliable observations) and SG11 (location-specific consensus gate with robust aggregation) are complementary. A single fixed combination is computed with no tuning: SG11's trim20/rho 0.80 rule applied only over SG12's top-50% observations. Success requires beating both parents, not just REF.
sg14.names: All class-word (W). REF = one pass; SG11/trim20/rho0p80 = frozen SG11 cell (20% trimmed mean where max(r_up, r_down) >= 0.80, else seed c); SG12/top50 = frozen SG12 cell (mean of the 124 most consistent of 248 observations). SG14 = among SG12's 124 retained observations, compute r_up/r_down and a 20% trimmed mean (24 removed per tail); use the trimmed mean where max(r_up, r_down) >= 0.80, else c. No CRF. 4 cells.
sg14.reference: Three screens: SG14 vs W/REF, vs W/SG11/trim20/rho0p80 and vs W/SG12/top50, plus a joint vote; success needed positive OOF and >= 4/5 votes against both parents.
sg14.outcome: SG14 froze against REF (5/5, OOF 0.798651 vs 0.787280) but each parent was retained 5/5 in its own screen (SG11 0.798400, SG12 0.796658), and the joint screen kept SG11; COCO SG14 0.621678 vs SG11 0.621916 and SG12 0.627174. The complementarity criterion is not met.

sg15.title: SG15 prior-driven SPEC32 region refinement
sg15.what: Instead of recognising the target from region statistics (SG13), SG15 uses an already-good pixelwise mask as the semantic prior and the fixed SPEC32 SA partition only as a spatial regulariser. Each region's fraction of prior-foreground pixels decides whether the region is projected to foreground, snapped, or left as is. Three frozen priors are refined separately, each at its own inherited threshold; Section 93 is a 20-image visual diagnostic of the same rules against the GT-majority oracle, not part of the table.
sg15.names: <prior>[/SG15-<rule>]; all class-word (W). Priors: P1 = two passes mean_i(A_i^2 c); SG11/trim20/rho0p80 and SG12/top50 = the frozen SG11 and SG12 cells; REF = one pass (control). For each SPEC32 region, f = fraction of its annotation-resolution pixels in the thresholded prior mask (threshold inherited from the unrefined prior, never re-selected). SG15-A025 / A050 / A075 = majority projection: the whole region is foreground if f >= q, q = 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75, else background (q chosen inside the VOC training folds in the A screen). SG15-B = confidence snapping: f >= 0.75 -> whole region foreground, f <= 0.25 -> whole region background, otherwise keep the prior's pixels. 16 cells.
sg15.reference: Each refinement is screened against its own unrefined prior (W/P1, W/SG11/trim20/rho0p80, W/SG12/top50): six screens (3 priors x A, B).
sg15.outcome: All six screens kept their prior 5/5. Best refinement SG11+B: OOF 0.798934 vs 0.798400, COCO 0.622023 vs 0.621916, no eligible vote; all A variants hurt OOF.

token_sg3_confirmation.title: Locked token-SG3 confirmation
token_sg3_confirmation.what: A locked confirmation of the strongest SG1/SG3 signal: the fixed token confidence-lock T/SG3/f95_b05_r0_n1, with and without OVAM's DenseCRF, against the one- and two-pass token references. No graph parameter is selected; only each fixed cell's mask threshold is chosen inside the folds.
token_sg3_confirmation.names: All on the T track (OVAM released optimized token, keys [<SoT>, token]). REF = observation-wise one SA pass; P1 = observation-wise two passes; SG3 = fixed confidence-locked candidate f95_b05_r0_n1: top-5% foreground and bottom-5% background anchors, no border band, one mean-graph step through SA module 15 with anchor values restored to the CA seed; +R2 = followed by OVAM's fixed DenseCRF. 6 cells.
token_sg3_confirmation.reference: Registered fixed comparisons: P1 vs REF, P1+R2 vs REF+R2, SG3 vs REF, SG3+R2 vs REF+R2, and SG3+R2 vs P1+R2; the key test is T/SG3+R2 vs T/REF+R2.
token_sg3_confirmation.outcome: T/SG3 vs T/REF OOF 0.8507 -> 0.8562 (+0.0056, paired +0.0059 [+0.0013, +0.0105]); T/SG3+R2 vs T/REF+R2 0.8643 -> 0.8674 (+0.0030, paired CI [-0.0020, +0.0076]); vs T/P1+R2 +0.0020 (CI crosses zero). COCO T/SG3+R2 0.7006 vs T/REF+R2 0.6850, transfer only; not promoted (Sections 78, 80).
token_sg3_confirmation.unsure: The package report.md and summary.json give only fixed-cell OOF comparisons, with no fold votes or 'frozen' field; the 'VOC does not promote it' decision is taken from protocol Sections 78 and 80.

sg17.title: SG17 reliability-filtered second-pass additions
sg17.what: Asks whether the second SA propagation pass can be kept only where the individual observations agree that it should add foreground. Seed is the frozen class-word CA map; the 248 observations are 31 calls x 8 heads of SA module 15. Where the second pass lowers the score it is kept as is; a raw increase is kept only at pixels where at least a cutoff fraction of observations increase from pass 1 to pass 2. The cutoff (top 30/20/10% of VOC positive-increment pixels) is the only thing varied; CRF was to run only if a candidate was promoted.
sg17.names: Prefix W/ = frozen training-free class-word CA seed. W/P1 = ordinary observation-wise two-pass map mean_i(A_i^2 c) over all 248 observations, calls 0-30 (in this older naming 'P1' is the two-pass map; SG22 later calls the same thing ALL-P2). W/SG17-Q70, -Q80, -Q90 = gated map y1 + min(y2-y1,0) + 1[q_up >= cutoff]*max(y2-y1,0), where y1 is the one-pass mean, y2 the two-pass mean and q_up the fraction of the 248 observations whose second-pass value exceeds the first; Q70/Q80/Q90 set the cutoff so that the top 30/20/10% of VOC positive-increment pixels pass. All three collapsed to the same cutoff (248/248 observations, 39.93% of increments retained), so the three rows are identical. No +R2 cells were run.
sg17.reference: W/P1, the ungated two-pass map, i.e. the existing method that the gate tries to improve.
sg17.outcome: W/P1 won all 5 VOC folds and was frozen; no SG17 cell promoted. Forced OOF 0.7991 vs 0.7998 (gain -0.0007), full VOC 0.8001 vs 0.8007, frozen COCO 0.6196 vs 0.6249; DenseCRF confirmation skipped because no cell was promoted.
sg17.unsure: The 0.7991 OOF value is quoted from protocol Section 97; report.md gives only the -0.0007 gain.

sg18_temporal_windowed.title: SG18 temporal-windowed one-pass propagation
sg18_temporal_windowed.what: Asks whether one-pass SA propagation improves when the per-observation maps are averaged over only part of the 31 denoising calls instead of all of them. Seed, SA module 15 and all 8 heads are fixed; only the call window changes (three preregistered windows). No CRF; the two-pass map is shown as an external benchmark but cannot win.
sg18_temporal_windowed.names: Prefix W/ = class-word CA seed. All cells are one-pass means of A_i c over the listed calls x 8 heads of SA module 15. W/REF = calls 0-30 (248 observations). W/T1 = calls 10-20 (88 observations; the 'middle' window, later called MID-P1). W/T2 = calls 10-30 (168). W/T3 = calls 6-30 (200, drops the first six calls). W/P1 = two-pass all-call map mean_i(A_i^2 c) (later ALL-P2), external benchmark only, not eligible for selection.
sg18_temporal_windowed.reference: W/REF, the one-pass all-call average the windows are meant to improve on.
sg18_temporal_windowed.outcome: W/T1 won 5/5 VOC folds and was promoted. OOF 0.7939 vs REF 0.7873 (+0.0066); full VOC 0.7959 vs 0.7886; frozen COCO 0.6285 vs 0.6172. T2 and T3 had positive forced OOF gains but 0/5 votes.

sg18_t1_crf.title: SG18 follow-up: T1 window + DenseCRF
sg18_t1_crf.what: Asks whether the promoted one-pass middle-window map (T1) plus the unchanged OVAM DenseCRF beats the established final pipeline, two-pass all-call propagation plus the same CRF (FTF). Four cells share each generated trajectory; no window or CRF parameter is selected.
sg18_t1_crf.names: Prefix W/ = class-word CA seed. W/T1 = one-pass mean over SA calls 10-20 x 8 heads of module 15 (SG18 winner; later MID-P1). W/P1 = two-pass all-call map mean_i(A_i^2 c), calls 0-30 (later ALL-P2). Suffix +R2 = the fixed OVAM DenseCRF on the thresholded mask. W/P1+R2 is FTF.
sg18_t1_crf.outcome: W/P1+R2 received 5/5 VOC fold votes; T1+R2 not promoted. Forced OOF 0.8106 vs 0.8135 (-0.0029); full VOC 0.8122 vs 0.8135; frozen COCO 0.6465 vs 0.6375 (transfer only).

sg21_structural.title: SG21 structural SA-head weighting
sg21_structural.what: Keeps the SG18/T1 setup (one pass, calls 10-20) but replaces the equal average over the 8 heads within each call with weights from a GT-free structural descriptor of each head's attention matrix. Four preregistered weightings; the 11 call outputs are still averaged equally. No CRF.
sg21_structural.names: SG18/T1 = equal-head one-pass mean, SA module 15, calls 10-20. SG21-LM = head weights proportional to raw radius-1 local attention mass. SG21-LM-RANK = weights proportional to ascending local-mass rank 1-8 (ties by physical head ID). SG21-ENT = weights proportional to (largest head entropy in that call - head's mean row entropy + 1e-8), favouring sharp heads. SG21-DIST = weights proportional to inverse mean query-key distance (+1e-8). Weights are normalized to sum to 1 within each call.
sg21_structural.reference: SG18/T1, same-generation; the method whose head average is being reweighted.
sg21_structural.outcome: T1 won 5/5 VOC folds; no structural weighting promoted. Forced OOF T1 0.7939, LM 0.7884, LM-RANK 0.7901, ENT 0.7872, DIST 0.7941 (+0.0002, below the promotion guard); DIST frozen COCO 0.6287 vs T1 0.6285.

sg22.title: SG22 call window x propagation depth factorial
sg22.what: Full factorial crossing the SA call window (all 31 calls vs middle calls 10-20) with propagation depth (1, 2 or 3 passes of each observation's own SA matrix), each scored raw and after the fixed DenseCRF. Seed is the class-word CA map; module 15, all 8 heads. Raw and CRF levels are screened separately.
sg22.names: Pattern WINDOW-Pk[+R2]. WINDOW: ALL = SA calls 0-30 (248 call/head observations); MID = calls 10-20 (88). Pk = mean over observations of A_i^k c, k = 1, 2, 3 passes (P1 = one pass, P2 = two passes, P3 = three). +R2 = fixed OVAM DenseCRF. Correspondences with older names: ALL-P1 = W/REF, ALL-P2 = old W/P1 (two-pass), ALL-P2+R2 = FTF, MID-P1 = SG18 W/T1, MID-P1+R2 = W/T1+R2. MID-P2+R2 is the operator used downstream from SG24 on.
sg22.reference: Raw: ALL-P2 (two-pass all-call map). CRF: ALL-P2+R2 (FTF, the final pipeline at the time).
sg22.outcome: Raw screen kept ALL-P2 (3/5 votes). CRF screen selected MID-P2+R2 (4/5 votes; selected OOF 0.8158 vs 0.8132); forced OOF 0.8168, full VOC 0.8185 vs 0.8132, frozen COCO 0.6438 vs 0.6372.

sg23.title: SG23 call window x reliability rule factorial
sg23.what: Asks whether three earlier reliability-based aggregation rules (SG2 graph, SG11 trimmed consensus, SG12 top-half observations) still help once propagation is restricted to the middle calls. 2 windows x 4 aggregation rules, all one pass, raw and after the fixed DenseCRF, plus a same-generation FTF reference outside the factorial.
sg23.names: Pattern WINDOW-RULE[+R2]. WINDOW: ALL = calls 0-30 (248 observations), MID = calls 10-20 (88). RULE (all one pass, module 15, 8 heads): R0 = ordinary mean of A_i c (MID-R0 = T1, ALL-R0 = REF); SG2 = locked consensus-edge graph G_cv_g20_n1, one pass through W = rownorm(mean_i A_i * r^2) with r = mean_i A_i / sqrt(mean_i A_i^2), i.e. each edge reweighted by its squared cross-observation agreement (gamma 2); SG11 = 20%-per-tail trimmed mean of the observation maps gated by directional consensus at rho 0.80; SG12 = mean of the top 50% observations by leave-one-out cosine (124 of 248 for ALL, 44 of 88 for MID). +R2 = fixed DenseCRF. ALL-P2 / ALL-P2+R2 = two-pass all-call map without / with CRF (ALL-P2+R2 = FTF), auxiliary references outside the factorial.
sg23.reference: Raw: MID-R0 (= SG18/T1). Final: ALL-P2+R2 (FTF). MID-R0+R2 is reported separately.
sg23.outcome: Raw screen selected MID-SG2 (5/5; OOF 0.7999 vs T1 0.7939; COCO 0.6292 vs 0.6287). CRF screen kept ALL-P2+R2 (4/5); no final cell promoted. Window x rule interactions are negative on VOC OOF and COCO.
sg23.unsure: Exact SG11 gating operator (how the rho 0.80 consensus gate combines with the trimmed mean) was taken from the protocol wording, not re-derived from code.

sg24_a.title: SG24-A automatic CA seed construction
sg24_a.what: Changes only how the CA seed is built from the selected 11 CA modules (calls 0-30, all heads), testing four automatic weighting schemes adapted from GoCA-style ideas against equal aggregation. Each variant is scored as a CA-only map and through the final pipeline (MID-P2 + R2).
sg24_a.names: Pattern Ak/LEVEL. Ak = CA construction: A0 = existing equal aggregation; A1 = per-pixel content-token mass rescaling (content tokens exclude special/padding tokens, punctuation and stopwords); A2 = projected-output CA head contribution weights (v_h = (A_h V_h) W_h^O, score s_h = v_h . sum_j v_j, GoCA dot-product normalization); A3 = pseudo-global / paired-SA similarity layer (module) weights: a pseudo-global map from the conditional Q of up_blocks.2.attentions.1 attn2 is compared with each layer's paired mean-head SA affinity, weights nonnegative and normalized within each call, calls averaged equally; A4 = A1+A2+A3 combined. LEVEL: /CA = CA-only seed map, thresholded directly (no SA, no CRF); /FINAL = seed -> MID-P2 (SA module 15, calls 10-20, 8 heads, two observation-wise passes) -> R2 DenseCRF.
sg24_a.reference: A0/CA and A0/FINAL, same generation; A0/FINAL reproduces SG22 MID-P2+R2.
sg24_a.outcome: CA-only screen kept A0 5/5; final screen kept A0 (A3 got 3/5 votes, selected-path OOF 0.81616 vs 0.81689). Forced A3/FINAL won 4/5 held-out folds, OOF 0.82297 vs 0.81689, full VOC 0.8243 vs 0.8185, COCO 0.6620 vs 0.6437; not a formal promotion, but the owner later adopted A3 -> MID-P2 -> R2 as the exploratory working default (protocol Section 103). A1/A4 score 0 on COCO because class-only prompts make content rescaling spatially constant. Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run.
sg24_a.unsure: Protocol Section 107 documents an implementation issue: A3's affinity similarity uses a transposed SA orientation relative to GoCA (scores M^T vs P). Section 114 measured it as changing per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% relative on four images. So A3 is a transposed GoCA-style adaptation, not a faithful GoCA weighting.

sg24_b.title: SG24-B CA module set: 11 vs all 16
sg24_b.what: Asks whether adding back the five excluded CA modules (including all 32x32 modules) helps when layer weights are set automatically by A3. Because SG24-A promoted no automatic method, the preregistered fallback A3 was used, so this package is diagnostic and cannot promote anything.
sg24_b.names: Pattern Bm-A3/LEVEL. B0 = the 11 selected CA modules; B1 = all 16 CA modules, including the 32x32 ones; -A3 = A3 automatic layer weighting (from SG24-A) recomputed over that module set; /CA = CA-only seed map; /FINAL = seed -> MID-P2 -> R2 (same as SG24-A).
sg24_b.reference: B0-A3/CA and B0-A3/FINAL, the 11-module A3 seed (same as SG24-A's A3 cells, regenerated).
sg24_b.outcome: B1-A3/FINAL lost all five VOC folds: OOF 0.8152 vs 0.8230, full VOC 0.8152 vs 0.8244; frozen COCO rose 0.6622 -> 0.6703 (transfer only, cannot override VOC). SG24-B is recorded as diagnostic (A3 fallback). Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run.
sg24_b.unsure: Per Section 107, the A3 transpose affects the 11 resized modules but not the five 32x32 modules, so B1 mixes two orientations; the reported ~31% weight on the 32x32 group is affected.

sg25.title: SG25 multi-resolution SA propagation (+ Pre-SG26 first-arrival diagnostic)
sg25.what: Asks whether coarser SA modules (16x16, 32x32), alone or paired with the fine 64x64 module, give better two-step propagation of the A3 seed than fine-only propagation. Each cell applies two propagation operations taken from the same diffusion call, with calls 10-20 and all heads; raw and after R2. The same run also records at which propagation depth (1-5) each fine-map pixel first becomes foreground (diagnostic only).
sg25.names: All cells: A3 CA seed, SA calls 10-20, all 8 heads, two propagation operations, output at 64x64. FINE-P2 = both passes with the 64x64 module 15 (= MID-P2; A3/FINE-P2+R2 is the working default). COARSE16-P2 / COARSE32-P2 = seed area-downsampled to 16x16 / 32x32, both passes with the final up-path SA module at that size, result bilinearly upsampled to 64. 16-to-64 / 32-to-64 (shown as 16->64, 32->64) = first pass with the 16 / 32 module (its heads averaged), upsample, second pass with each 64x64 head. 64-to-16 = first pass 64x64, area-downsample, second pass 16x16, upsample. Modules: up_blocks.1/.2/.3 .attentions.2.transformer_blocks.0.attn1 for 16/32/64. +R2 = fixed DenseCRF.
sg25.reference: FINE-P2 and FINE-P2+R2, the existing fine-only operator (same generation).
sg25.outcome: Raw and R2 screens kept the fine reference in all five folds; nothing promoted. FINE-P2+R2 0.82425 VOC / 0.66210 COCO. Frozen COCO favoured 16-to-64+R2 (0.6975) and COARSE32-P2+R2 (0.6948), but both lost on VOC (forced OOF 0.8170 and 0.8138 vs 0.8228). First-arrival TP rate fell with depth: VOC 0.865 -> 0.223, COCO 0.708 -> 0.117 (depth 1 -> 5). Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run.

sg26.title: SG26 coarse-gated fine SA
sg26.what: Asks whether coarse SA can constrain fine SA without replacing it: the fine 64x64 attention matrices are multiplied elementwise by a gate lifted from the coarse (16 or 32) attention of the same call, then row-normalized. The gate is used on both passes or only on the second; raw and after R2, A3 seed, calls 10-20.
sg26.names: S0 = FINE-P2 (two ordinary 64x64 passes). S1 = SG25 16-to-64. S2 = SG25 32-to-64 (repeat controls). Gated operator: per call, average the 8 coarse attention matrices at 16 (or 32), block-lift to the 64x64 grid (each fine pixel mapped to its coarse cell), multiply each fine head's matrix elementwise by the lifted gate, row-normalize. S3 / S4 = 16- / 32-gated fine SA on both passes. S5 / S6 = ordinary fine pass 1, then 16- / 32-gated fine pass 2. +R2 = fixed DenseCRF. These S numbers are unrelated to SG27's, except that S0-S2 are the same base maps.
sg26.reference: S0 and S0+R2 (FINE-P2, the working default).
sg26.outcome: Raw and R2 screens chose S0 in 5/5 folds; no gate promoted. Final VOC/COCO: S0 0.8242/0.6621, S3 0.7992/0.6817, S4 0.7993/0.6746, S5 0.8201/0.6821, S6 0.8193/0.6773. Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run.

sg27.title: SG27 late fusion of three SA output maps
sg27.what: Asks whether a fixed, parameter-free pixelwise combination of three completed propagation maps (fine, 16->64, 32->64 from SG25) beats the fine map alone. Only the fusion formula varies (46 proposed, 42 numerically unique); every fused map is scored raw and after R2. No coarse attention modifies the fine SA matrices.
sg27.names: Base maps, each min-max normalized before fusion: F = FINE-P2 (= S0), C16 = 16-to-64 (= S1), C32 = 32-to-64 (= S2); every fused map is min-max normalized again; +R2 = fixed DenseCRF. Pairwise operators in a fixed order: mean, geometric mean sqrt(ab), harmonic 2ab/(a+b+eps), RMS, max, min, product ab, soft OR a+b-ab, agreement-weighted first map a(1-|a-b|), agreement-weighted mean ((a+b)/2)(1-|a-b|). F with C16: S3 mean, S4 geometric, S5 harmonic, S6 RMS, S7 max, S8 min, S9 product, S10 soft OR, S13 F(1-|F-C16|), S14 agreement-weighted mean. F with C32: S16 mean, S17 geometric, S18 harmonic, S19 RMS, S20 max, S21 min, S22 product, S23 soft OR, S25 F(1-|F-C32|), S26 agreement-weighted mean. C16 with C32 (no fine map): S27 mean, S28 geometric, S29 harmonic, S30 max, S31 min, S32 soft OR. All three maps: S33 mean, S34 geometric (cube root of product), S35 harmonic, S36 RMS, S37 max, S38 min, S39 soft OR 1-(1-F)(1-C16)(1-C32), S40 median, S41 mean of the top two, S42 mean of the bottom two. Fine-anchored: S43 F(1-|F-(C16+C32)/2|), S44 F*sqrt((1-|F-C16|)(1-|F-C32|)), S45 max(F, (C16+C32)/2). S11, S12, S15, S24 were exact duplicates (S11 = S15 = S7, S12 = S8, S24 = S20) and were dropped, leaving 42 unique cells (84 with +R2), numbered S0-S45 with gaps.
sg27.reference: S0 / S0+R2 = FINE-P2 alone (the working default, A3 -> FINE-P2 -> R2).
sg27.outcome: Raw and R2 multi-candidate VOC screens selected S0 in 5/5 folds; S0+R2 stays at 0.8242 VOC / 0.6621 COCO. S8+R2 (F/C16 min) had the best full VOC (0.8258) and S38+R2 (three-way min) the best forced OOF (0.8256, +0.0028), both below the promotion gate. S9+R2 (F x C16 product) reached 0.7054 frozen COCO but lost VOC (forced OOF 0.8123; VOC threshold 0.300 at the grid edge). Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run.
sg27.unsure: The brief said S0..S41, but the cell names actually run S0-S45 with S11, S12, S15, S24 missing (42 unique cells). The handoff notes that S4 (geometric) and S9 (product) rank pixels identically and differ only through the discrete threshold grid. Inherits the A3 orientation caveat.

sg28.title: SG28 PEARL-inspired components (Procrustes alignment, Laplacian smoothing)
sg28.what: Tests two independent, never-combined components adapted from PEARL on top of the working default A3 -> FINE-P2. (a) Recompute module-15 SA after per-head Q/K centering and/or Procrustes alignment of keys to queries. (b) Smooth the final normalized score on a 64x64 grid graph, optionally with image-boundary edge weights and/or cross-scale confidence. Raw and after R2.
sg28.names: P0 = exact historical A3 -> FINE-P2 map (SA module 15, calls 10-20, 8 heads, two observation-wise passes). Caution: here P1-P3 are Procrustes variants, not propagation depths. PA branch: P1 = weighted query-norm centering then SVD Procrustes rotation K -> Q (rotation applied to uncentered K); P2 = weighted centering only; P3 = uniform centering then SVD Procrustes. Laplacian branch, solving (D_rho + L)F = D_rho f on the 4-neighbour grid with f = normalized P0 score: B1 = unit edges, rho = 1; B2 = image-boundary edge weights exp(-5|I_i - I_j|) from the grayscale generated image, rho = 1; C1 / C2 / C3 = unit edges with confidence rho = 1-|f-c16|, 1-|f-c32|, or 1 minus the average three-scale pairwise disagreement (c16/c32 = the coarse-path maps); D1 / D2 / D3 = the same rho with B2's boundary edges. +R2 = fixed DenseCRF.
sg28.outcome: Every selector kept P0 (raw) and P0+R2 (final) in 5/5 VOC folds; nothing promoted. Baseline after R2 0.8228 forced OOF / 0.8242 full VOC / 0.6621 COCO. Best component B2: raw forced OOF 0.8140 (+0.0043, below the +0.005 floor), raw COCO 0.6654; after R2 0.8230 (+0.0001) and COCO 0.6661. Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run. Independent audit (protocol Sec. 130): all 24 cells recomputed from the per-image shards match the report; P0 and P0+R2 equal the historical SG27 S0 counts on all 490 VOC and 707 COCO images. The +0.005 floor applies to each fold's training gain, which for B2 is only +0.0017 to +0.0030. Raw B2 on COCO gains +0.0068 [+0.0050, +0.0086] in paired mean image IoU; after R2 the interval includes zero. Centering K cancels in the softmax, so P2 is effectively query centering only; the cross-scale trust saturates because all three maps share the final fine-scale pass from the same seed.

sg29.title: SG29 NERVE-inspired head weighting and stopped random walk
sg29.what: Adapts three ideas from NERVE to the working default A3 -> FINE-P2: class-conditioned head weights from the spatial entropy of each head's one-step output, a geometrically stopped random walk instead of exactly two passes, and a local Q/K 8-neighbour transition fused with the global SA. Seven main cells, raw and after R2, plus three walk-length diagnostics. Single-class spatial entropy replaces NERVE's multiclass entropy, so this is an adaptation, not a reproduction.
sg29.names: All cells: historical A3 CA seed, SA module 15 at 64x64, calls 10-20, 8 heads; global transitions are the original SD softmax SA. N0 = exact historical observation-wise two-pass map (FINE-P2; = SG28 P0). N1 = N0 with class-conditioned head weights softmax(-3H) within each call, H = spatial entropy of the head's one-step output divided by log(4096). N2 = geometrically stopped walk sum_{d=0..10} 0.9^d A^d c / sum_d 0.9^d per head, heads averaged. N3 = the same walk on a local transition only (8-neighbour (cos(Q,K)+1)/2 + 1e-6, plus 0.01 self weight, row-normalized). N4 = walk on the fused transition 0.8 x global + 0.2 x local. N5 = N1 head weights + N2 walk. N6 = N4 walk + entropy head weights computed from the fused one-step output. N2-L1 / N2-L2 / N2-L5 = N2 truncated at walk length 1 / 2 / 5 (diagnostic only, not selectable). +R2 = fixed DenseCRF.
sg29.reference: N0 / N0+R2, the exact historical working default (checked per image against same-generation FINE-P2; SG28 counts were a replay audit only).
sg29.outcome: Every selector kept N0 (raw) and N0+R2 (final) in 5/5 VOC folds; nothing promoted. N0+R2: 0.8229 forced OOF / 0.8243 full VOC / 0.6623 COCO. N1+R2 won 5/5 pairwise folds but gained only +0.0001 forced OOF; entropy weights are near uniform (7.998/8 effective heads) and do not rank heads within a call. Stopped walks trade VOC for COCO: N2+R2 0.8135 / 0.8147 / 0.6696, N4+R2 0.8103 / 0.8110 / 0.6704, N6+R2 0.8104 / 0.8110 / 0.6705; N4+R2's COCO gain loses 0.0356 person IoU and its paired mean-image interval crosses zero. Local-only N3+R2 fails (0.7278 / 0.7278 / 0.6118). Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run. Owner-reported; not yet independently audited.

pre_sg16_sg17.title: Pre-SG16 / Pre-SG17 region and second-pass diagnostics
pre_sg16_sg17.what: Diagnostic only (no method selected). Pre-SG16 asks whether any GT-free region statistic can tell which SPEC32 regions are really foreground, especially regions where the P1 prior is ambiguous (occupancy 0.2-0.8), scored by region ROC-AUC against a GT-majority label. Pre-SG17 asks whether observation agreement predicts whether a pixel change made by the second SA pass is useful (FN->TP, FP->TN) or harmful, at fixed threshold 0.45. Run on all 490 VOC / 707 COCO images.
pre_sg16_sg17.names: Region features: p1/sg11/sg12_occupancy = fraction of the region marked foreground by the frozen P1 (two-pass), SG11 or SG12 prior mask; occupancy_mean/max = across the three priors; ca_mean, p1_mean = mean raw score in the region; obs_all_* / obs_top50_* = a statistic (mean, median, trim20, r_max directional consensus, etc.) of the per-observation region means over all 248 observations or the SG12 top-124. Subsets: all, ambiguous_p1, wrong_p1, priors_agree/disagree. Pixel signals: second_q_direction = fraction of observations whose second pass moves in the proposed direction; *_median/_trim10_direction = median/trimmed change; top50_* = same on top-124 observations; support_reliability = SG12 reliability of supporting observations; first_r_max = first-pass consensus.

sg30.title: SG30 SPARK-inspired nonlinear affinity sharpening
sg30.what: Adapts SPARK's expansion, inflation and pruning of a random-walk graph to the fine SA graph of A3 -> FINE-P2 (module 15, calls 10-20, 8 heads, observation-wise). Varies where an elementwise power r = 2.6 is applied, whether A is first expanded to A^2, pruning at tau = 1e-7, and one feature-local/global fused update. Constants are fixed from the paper, no sweep; author code was unavailable, so the local graph is an explicit adaptation. Eight cells raw and after R2, plus two raw iteration diagnostics.
sg30.names: Infl(X) = elementwise power X^2.6 then row normalization. S0 = historical observation-wise P2 mean_i(A_i^2 c) (same-generation FINE-P2). S1 = Infl(A) used for both passes. S2 = ordinary first pass, Infl(A) on the second pass. S3 = Infl(A^2) applied once to c. S4 = ordinary first pass Ac, then Infl(A^2). S5 = S3 with entries of the unnormalized power below tau = 1e-7 pruned and rows renormalized (an emptied row falls back to its pre-pruned row). S6 = S4 with the same pruning. S7 = one SPARK-like update (expand, inflate, prune) on 0.6 x global SA + 0.4 x a local graph from module-15 input features (after group norm, before Q/K/V; negative cosine clamped to 0, self weight 1, row-normalized), applied to c. S5-I2 / S5-I3 = the S5 update repeated two / three times (raw diagnostics only). +R2 = fixed DenseCRF. Caution: apart from S0 = FINE-P2, S cells here are unrelated to SG31's or SG32's same-numbered cells; SG30 S2 reappears as SG32 S1.
sg30.reference: S0 / S0+R2 = same-generation FINE-P2, the working default.
sg30.outcome: Every selector kept S0 (raw) and S0+R2 (final) in 5/5 VOC folds; nothing promoted. S0+R2: 0.8231 forced OOF / 0.8244 full VOC / 0.6623 COCO. Second-pass inflation S2+R2 reached 0.6855 COCO but 0.8125 forced OOF (1/5 pairwise wins) / 0.8156 full VOC; S6+R2 0.8144 / 0.8144 / 0.6836; S4+R2 0.8187 / 0.8200 / 0.6732. S1, S5 and feature-local S7 (S7+R2 0.7356 / 0.7356 / 0.6206) fail. Inflation concentrates mass (top-quartile edge mass 0.825 -> 0.976), yet graph purity does not predict masks; S6 pruning removes about 99% of entries. S2 trades recall for precision. Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run. Owner-reported; not yet independently audited.
sg30.unsure: The later calibration audit (Sec. 125) found the S2+R2 / S6+R2 COCO gains vanish at matched thresholds; not folded into this outcome.

sg31.title: SG31 SeeDiff-inspired re-seeding and background propagation
sg31.what: Adapts SeeDiff's coarse-to-fine re-seeding and explicit background expansion to A3 with the SG25 16/32/64 SA modules (same call, calls 10-20, 8 heads). Hard 0.5 seed sets from SeeDiff are expanded by averaging selected SA rows, then re-thresholded scale by scale; separate cells gate the fine map by propagated background support. Includes historical controls and a score-squaring control. Eleven cells raw and after R2. A shard stopped on a too-tight float tolerance in the S1 control and was resumed after relaxing it.
sg31.names: F = normalized fine map; selected-row expansion E(S) = mean over p in S of head-mean A[p,:] (SeeDiff orientation, not A @ c); every scale step is spatially min-max normalized. S0 = same-generation FINE-P2. S1 = historical SG25 16->64 continuous path. S2 = continuous 16->32->64 (three same-call SA applications). S3 = hard selected-row re-seeding 16->32->64 (seed = normalized map > 0.5 at each scale; empty sets fall back to top-1). S4 = the same hard re-seeding 32->64 only. S5 = soft control, rows weighted by the nonnegative score, 16->32->64. Background seeds F <= 0.5; B = their normalized support; gated maps are minmax(F(1-B)). S6 = S0 gated by one-step selected-row B. S7 = S0 gated by observation-wise A64^2 background. S8 / S9 = S3 / S4 gated by selected-row B. S10 = normalized F^2 (monotone sharpening control). +R2 = fixed DenseCRF. Caution: apart from S0 = FINE-P2, S cells are unrelated to SG30's or SG32's same-numbered cells; SG31 S2 is the ordinary hierarchy replayed as SG33 H0, SG-combined-v1 C1 and v2 V1.
sg31.reference: S0 / S0+R2 = same-generation FINE-P2, the working default.
sg31.outcome: Every selector kept S0 (raw) and S0+R2 (final) in 5/5 VOC folds; nothing promoted. S0+R2: 0.8228 forced OOF / 0.8243 full VOC / 0.6622 COCO. Historical S1+R2: 0.8170 / 0.8183 / 0.6977; continuous S2+R2: 0.8182 / 0.8193 / 0.6923. Hard re-seeding collapses recall (S3+R2 0.2122 / 0.2122 / 0.2606; seed fraction 30.9% at 16x16 -> 6.4% at 64x64 on VOC). Background S6+R2 0.8199 / 0.8209 / 0.6757; score squaring S10+R2 0.7968 / 0.7968 / 0.6855, matching S7's COCO gain and weakening the case that propagated background is distinctive. Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run. Owner-reported; not yet independently audited.

sg32.title: SG32 reliability-adaptive second SA pass
sg32.what: An original hypothesis from SG22/SG27/SG30/SG31: keep the first fine pass u = A c and sharpen the second pass only where a per-pixel reliability signal is low. Reliability comes from cross-scale agreement of first-pass maps (16/32/64) and/or selected-row background support, per call and shared across the 8 heads. Two forms: convex blend of ordinary and sharpened second passes, or a row-wise exponent. Twelve cells raw and after R2; no sweep.
sg32.names: A^sharp = row-wise power 2.6, row-normalized (SG30). Per call, f, m, k = separately min-max normalized head-mean first-pass maps at 64, 32->64 and 16->64. Reliability R (clamped to [0,1]): c16 = 1-|f-k|; pair = 1 - mean of the three pairwise |differences|; range = 1 - (max - min) of the three; bg = 1 - B, with B = normalized mean SA row over first-pass background seeds f <= 0.5; pair x bg; range x bg. S0 = ordinary P2, A u = A(Ac) (= FINE-P2). S1 = SG30-S2 fixed sharpening, A^sharp u. Convex cells R x A u + (1-R) x A^sharp u: S2 c16, S3 pair, S4 bg, S5 pair x bg, S6 range x bg. Row-temperature cells, per-row exponent r = 1 + 1.6(1-R) then row normalization: S7 c16, S8 pair, S9 bg, S10 pair x bg, S11 range x bg. Low reliability means more sharpening. +R2 = fixed DenseCRF. Caution: apart from S0 = FINE-P2, S cells are unrelated to SG30's or SG31's same-numbered cells.
sg32.reference: S0 / S0+R2 = same-generation FINE-P2, the working default.
sg32.outcome: Every selector kept S0 (raw) and S0+R2 (final) in 5/5 VOC folds; nothing promoted. S0+R2: 0.8229 forced OOF / 0.8243 full VOC / 0.6622 COCO. Best new cell S7+R2 (c16 temperature): 0.8234 forced OOF (+0.0005, 2/5 pairwise wins) / 0.8248 / 0.6773. The highest COCO cell is the historical sharpening control S1+R2 (0.8122 / 0.8153 / 0.6854), which loses 0.0107 forced OOF. Three-scale agreement saturates on distant background; background support is more spatially discriminative, but no adaptive combination clears the VOC rule. The same-generation control tolerance was set to atol 1e-5, rtol 1e-4. Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run. Owner-reported; not yet independently audited.

sg33.title: SG33 hierarchical residuals and coarse Markov reachability
sg33.what: Adapts FA-Seg (retain intermediate SA resolutions as residual support) and M2N2 (Markov first-arrival maps, IPF balancing, temperature 0.65) to the sequential 16->32->64 SA hierarchy seeded by A3 (matched SG25 modules, calls 10-20, 8 heads). Residual cells fuse normalized stage maps; Markov cells replace only the 16x16 start with a class-seeded reachability map. Twelve cells raw and after R2; no sweep; not a reproduction of either paper.
sg33.names: S0 = same-generation FINE-P2. Per call, r16, r32, r64 = min-max normalized stages of the ordinary head-mean 16->32->64 hierarchy, upsampled to 64. H0 = ordinary hierarchy (replays SG31 S2). H1 = (r16+r32+r64)/3; H2 = 0.2 r16 + 0.3 r32 + 0.5 r64; H3 = r16/9 + 5 r32/9 + 3 r64/9; H4 = max(r64, 0.5 r32, 0.25 r16). Markov start on the 16x16 head-mean SA transition from the normalized CA seed: a node's arrival is the first step (step 0 included) at which its walk probability exceeds 0.3 x the maximum, unreached nodes get the cap 256, support = 1 - normalized arrival; the support then runs the ordinary 16->32->64 path. M1 = ordinary transition; M2 = IPF-balanced transition (tolerance 1e-5, at most 100 iterations); M3 = rows sharpened at T = 0.65 before IPF. C1 / C2 / C3 = M1 / M2 / M3 plus the equal three-stage residual. +R2 = fixed DenseCRF. Caution: these C1-C3 are unrelated to SG-combined-v1's C1-C3, and M2 is unrelated to an earlier backlog cell named M2; SG-combined C10a replays SG33 M2.
sg33.reference: S0 / S0+R2 = same-generation FINE-P2, the working default.
sg33.outcome: The raw selector froze M2 with 4/5 votes (a raw-stage promotion; selected OOF 0.8159 vs 0.8098). M2: 0.8216 forced OOF (5/5 pairwise wins) / 0.8226 full VOC / 0.6463 COCO vs S0 0.8098 / 0.8114 / 0.6599; its threshold 0.675 sits near the grid top and the gain does not transfer. The final stage stayed at the reference: S0+R2 5/5 (0.8229 / 0.8243 / 0.6623); M2+R2 had 0.8313 forced OOF / 0.8313 / 0.6528 but only 3/5 pairwise wins and no votes. Residual H3+R2 reached 0.6976 COCO but 0.8106 / 0.8126 VOC (0/5). Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run. Owner-reported; not yet independently audited.

sg_combined_v1.title: SG-combined-v1 constrained transport and budgeted completion
sg_combined_v1.what: Our own unified mechanism, not a paper reproduction: coarse class evidence should be conserved through 16->32->64 refinement, and new evidence from a second fine SA pass admitted only under a background-aware budget. Each 2x2 child group is projected onto its coarse parent's mass with the closed-form KL solution (exact or 0.5-relaxed), then optional positive-residual completion. A3 seed, matched SA calls 10-20, 8 heads. Ten cells raw and after R2; no sweep.
sg_combined_v1.names: C0 = same-generation FINE-P2. C1 = ordinary 16->32->64 hierarchy, no conservation (replays SG31 S2; raw call maps averaged, then normalized). Transport cells work on per-call sum-normalized distributions; KL projection z_child = q_child x parent mass / sum of the group's q (uniform fallback when the group mass is near zero); min-max scoring only after transport. C2 = exact projection at 16->32 only. C3 = exact at 32->64 only. C4 = exact at both. C5 = 0.5-relaxed (half proposal, half exact) at both. Completion on a core: P1 = normalized core, P2 = normalized same-call head-mean fine SA applied to P1, residual [P2-P1]_+. C6 = C4 then unconditional second fine pass (P2). C7 = C4 + (1-B) x residual, B = SG32 selected-row background support. C8 = C4 + odds P1/(P1+B) x residual. C9 = C5 with the C8 rule. +R2 = fixed DenseCRF. Caution: these C1-C3 differ from SG33's C1-C3.
sg_combined_v1.reference: C0 / C0+R2 = same-generation FINE-P2, the working default.
sg_combined_v1.outcome: Every selector kept C0 (raw) and C0+R2 (final) in 5/5 VOC folds; nothing promoted. C0: 0.8097 forced OOF / 0.8114 full VOC / 0.6599 COCO; C0+R2: 0.8228 / 0.8242 / 0.6622. Exact both-scale C4 fell to 0.7592 / 0.7592 / 0.6499; relaxed C5 recovered to 0.7926, unconditional completion C6 to 0.8035; budgeted C8 was 0.7774. After R2, C6+R2 0.8201 / 0.8221 / 0.7063 and C8+R2 0.8031 / 0.8046 / 0.7061: large COCO gains, not selected on VOC. KL mass/ratio checks passed; preserving high-scoring wrong coarse parents plausibly drives C4's loss, and the fixed budget discards useful TP additions. Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run. Owner-reported; not yet independently audited.

sg_combined_c10.title: SG-combined-v1 C10 add-on: SG33 M2 coarse source
sg_combined_c10.what: Three cells added after SG33 completed, without changing SG-combined-v1's ten cells: they start the 16->32->64 hierarchy from SG33 M2's IPF-balanced 16x16 first-arrival source and test ordinary propagation, exact two-transition KL projection, and background-odds completion. Only C10a/b/c are candidates; a same-generation S0 is the reference. Raw and after R2; VOC-only selection, frozen COCO transfer; no new parameter.
sg_combined_c10.names: S0 = same-generation FINE-P2 (reference only, not a candidate). C10a = SG33 M2 source through ordinary same-call 16->32->64 SA (verified against same-generation SG33 M2). C10b = the same source with exact parentwise KL projection at 16->32 and 32->64 (SG-combined-v1 C4 operator). C10c = C10b plus the SG32 background-row / foreground-odds positive completion (SG-combined-v1 C8 rule). A second fine pass on C10b is a completion-efficiency diagnostic only. +R2 = fixed DenseCRF.
sg_combined_c10.reference: S0 / S0+R2 = same-generation FINE-P2, the working default.
sg_combined_c10.outcome: The raw selector froze C10a with 4/5 votes (a raw-stage promotion; selected OOF gain +0.0061). C10a: 0.8216 forced OOF (5/5 pairwise wins) / 0.8226 full VOC / 0.6465 COCO vs S0 0.8098 / 0.8114 / 0.6599; its threshold 0.675 sits near the grid top and COCO is worse. The final stage stayed at the reference: S0+R2 5/5 (0.8231 / 0.8244 / 0.6623); C10a+R2 0.8313 / 0.8313 / 0.6529, 3/5 pairwise wins. C10b collapses (0.6444 / 0.6473 / 0.5150; 64x64 stage AUC 0.975 -> 0.888); C10c recovers partly (0.7622). M2 stays excluded from v2. Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run. Owner-reported; not yet independently audited.

calibration_ap_audit.title: Calibration and ranking audit of SG25-SG-combined-v1 (diagnostic only)
calibration_ap_audit.what: A CPU-only re-read of the stored per-image counts of all 204 cells (raw and R2) of SG25, SG27, SG30, SG31, SG32, SG33 and SG-combined-v1, asking whether COCO transfer gains reflect better spatial ranking or only threshold calibration. Each cell's frozen transfer is set beside a label-using best-threshold mIoU and a threshold-free raw-map AP. No image is regenerated; no result, threshold, selection or promotion changes.
calibration_ap_audit.names: Frozen = registered result (VOC-selected threshold transferred unchanged to COCO). Best-threshold = cell and reference each take their best of the 17 thresholds on that dataset's own labels (optimistic, never a result; VOC is in-sample). Raw AP = mean per-image average precision of the raw 64x64 map with 20k paired bootstrap; threshold free, undefined for binary R2 masks. Gap = reference's COCO best-threshold minus frozen mIoU. Every delta is against the same package's same-stage reference. Cells: SG25 FINE-P2 (reference), COARSE32-P2 (both passes at 32x32, upsampled), 16-to-64 and 32-to-64 (coarse first pass, fine second pass); SG27 S0 (reference = FINE-P2), S8 (fine/16 min), S9 (fine x 16 product), S38 (three-way min); SG30 S0, S2 (second-pass inflation), S6 (S4 + pruning); SG31 S0, S1 (= SG25 16-to-64), S2 (continuous 16->32->64), S6 / S7 (background-gated), S10 (score squared); SG32 S0, S1 (fixed sharpening), S7 (c16 temperature); SG33 S0, H0 (ordinary hierarchy), H2 / H3 (stage residuals), M2 (IPF Markov source); SG-combined-v1 C0 (reference), C1 (ordinary hierarchy), C2 (exact KL 16->32), C5 (relaxed both), C6 (exact both + completion), C8 (exact both + odds budget). +R2 = fixed DenseCRF. The same S ids mean different operators in different packages.
calibration_ap_audit.reference: Each package's same-stage reference: FINE-P2 / S0 / C0 (raw vs raw, R2 vs R2).
calibration_ap_audit.outcome: Diagnostic only; every recomputed frozen mIoU matches the registered value to 1e-9. The fine reference is miscalibrated on COCO in every package: VOC threshold 0.425 (R2) / 0.45 (raw) vs COCO best 0.525, worth +0.027 / +0.020 mIoU. Hierarchy cells keep a COCO gain at matched thresholds (after R2: SG25 16->64 +0.022, SG33 H2/H3 +0.021/+0.020, C2 +0.024, C6 +0.026) and raw AP rises for 16->64, H2/H3 and C2. Sharpening wins (SG30 S2, SG32 S1) fall to about 0.000 and SG31 S6/S7/S10 to <= 0; S10's AP delta is exactly 0. C5/C6/C8 gain after R2 while raw AP falls; SG33 M2 ranks worse (COCO AP -0.037). Of 53 R2 cells with frozen COCO gain >= +0.015, 34 keep it at matched thresholds. Owner-reported; not yet independently audited.

sg_combined_v2.title: SG-combined-v2 one-sided coarse caps and route diagnostic
sg_combined_v2.what: Following the calibration audit, replaces the exact two-sided KL projection with a one-sided cap: children may not exceed their coarse parent's mass, clipped mass is discarded, and raw call weights are kept, so the cap is isolated against the ordinary hierarchy. Tests the cap at 16->32 and at both transitions, two completion variants, and a non-selectable per-image route diagnostic. A3 seed, matched SA calls 10-20, 8 heads. Seven cells raw and after R2.
sg_combined_v2.names: Cap on 2x2 groups: z_j = q_j x min(1, p_g / (mean_{k in g} q_k + 1e-12)), the generalized-KL projection onto upper-mass constraints, applied to the raw (unrenormalized) hierarchy maps. V0 = same-generation FINE-P2 (reference). V1 = ordinary raw 16->32->64 hierarchy (SG31 S2, v1 C1). V2 = v1 C6 replay (exact KL at both transitions + unconditional completion). V3 = cap at 16->32 only. V4 = cap at 16->32 and 32->64 (capped 32x32 map as parent). V5 = V3 core + unconditional completion (C6 convention). V6 = V3 core + whole positive residual admitted only where P1 >= B (B = SG32 background support). Route score R = sum B_i [F_i - H_i]_+ / (sum [F_i - H_i]_+ + 1e-8), primary pair F = V0, H = V2; E = fine-exclusive mean (secondary). +R2 = fixed DenseCRF. Caution: SG-A3G reuses V0 and V3 with the same meaning.
sg_combined_v2.reference: V0 / V0+R2 = same-generation FINE-P2, the working default.
sg_combined_v2.outcome: Every selector kept V0 (raw) and V0+R2 (final) in 5/5 VOC folds; nothing promoted. V0+R2: 0.8231 forced OOF / 0.8244 full VOC / 0.6622 COCO. V3+R2: 0.8304 forced OOF (+0.0073, 5/5 pairwise wins, paired interval [+0.0017, +0.0125]) / 0.8304 / 0.6966. V3 was ineligible: the worst class (sheep, -0.092 after R2) failed the -0.050 guard in every fold. The cap binds in 58% of groups but removes only 7.6% of mass, changing mask extent rather than ranking. V4 adds nothing; completion re-adds false positives (V5+R2 0.8209 / 0.8230 / 0.6647). Route AUC 0.554 VOC / 0.594 COCO: no-go. Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run. Owner-reported; not yet independently audited.
sg_combined_v2.unsure: Section 128's CPU diagnosis (sheep loss is recall on frame-filling objects, already present in the uncapped hierarchy) is not folded into this outcome. V3+R2 is described as the strongest structural cell so far but is not protocol-promoted.

sg_a3g.title: SG-A3G GoCA-oriented A3 seed and paired rerun
sg_a3g.what: Tests the open A3 orientation caveat directly. One diffusion run accumulates both the historical A3 seed and A3G, whose SA similarity uses GoCA's orientation; the two differ only in per-call CA module weights of resized modules, giving an exactly paired comparison per image. Each seed feeds the working default and the v2 V3 capped hierarchy. Pre-fixed questions: does G0+R2 - V0+R2 exceed the +/-0.002 tie band, and does V3's gain survive the corrected seed?
sg_a3g.names: V0 = historical A3 -> FINE-P2 (reference; same as SG-combined-v2 V0). V3 = historical A3 -> v2 V3 (one-sided cap at 16->32). G0 = A3G -> FINE-P2. G3 = A3G -> v2 V3. A3G = A3 with GoCA's affinity orientation <M,P> instead of the historical <M^T,P>. +R2 = fixed DenseCRF. Candidates V3, G0, G3.
sg_a3g.outcome: Registered and submitted (protocol Sec. 128); results pending. A two-image smoke shows the seeds barely differ (mean |A3G - A3| 0.0005 / 0.0010, Pearson r ~1.0); this is an execution check, not a result. If G0+R2 - V0+R2 exceeds the tie band, A3's descendants are owed a rerun on A3G; otherwise the historical results stand with the orientation documented.
sg_a3g.unsure: Section 128 also holds a completed CPU sheep / dining-table diagnosis of v2 V3 (diagnostic only); it is not reported here.

sg_combined_v3.title: SG-combined-v3 single changes to the V3 capped hierarchy
sg_combined_v3.what: Three owner-approved hypotheses, each changing exactly one thing relative to v2 V3: a per-head cap, a native coarse CA seed for the 16x16 start, and a temporal cap across SA calls. Seed is historical A3; SA calls 10-20; cap clipped mass discarded. Five cells raw and after R2, a mechanism table against V3, fixed decision rules, GT cap-loss diagnostics and an owner-approved dense-map sidecar aimed at the frame-filling recall loss.
sg_combined_v3.names: R0 = FINE-P2 (= v2 V0), the registered selection reference. R1 = v2 V3 replay: r16 = head-mean 16x16 SA x c16, z32 = cap of the 32x32 head-mean pass against r16, then head-mean 64x64 pass; local mechanism reference. W1 = per-head cap: z32 = mean over heads of cap(r16, A^32_h U r16) with the head-mean parent (removes at least as much mass as R1). W2 = native coarse seed: the R1 chain starts from c16* = minmax of the A3 CA contributions at <= 16x16 modules (unchanged A3 weights), so 64-px CA no longer enters the hierarchy. W3 = temporal cap: each call's R1 map is capped by the area-downsampled mean of earlier calls' maps (first call uncapped). +R2 = fixed DenseCRF. Caution: R0/R1 are new names for v2 V0/V3.
sg_combined_v3.reference: R0 / R0+R2 (selection reference, = v2 V0); R1 is the mechanism reference for W1-W3.
sg_combined_v3.outcome: Registered and submitted (protocol Sec. 129), chained behind SG-A3G; results pending. Pre-fixed rules: W2 becomes a final-method candidate if it beats R1 in >= 4/5 folds with the paired interval above zero and VOC sheep does not fall; W1 closes if sheep falls vs R1; W3 closes unless it beats R1 in >= 4/5 folds with the interval above zero. Caveat: A3's SA similarity uses a transposed affinity orientation relative to GoCA (protocol Sec. 107); on four images the correction changes per-call module weights by 0.9-2.0% (Sec. 114), and a corrected replay has not been run.
